stories.headline: AI self-improvement fears sharpen safety debate
stories.summary: AI-lab leaders called for a development pause as recursive self-improvement appears closer. Reuters notes no major intentional harm by AI, and critics question whether safety warnings could also strengthen incumbents through regulation.

stories.headline: Investors reassess the AI spending boom
stories.summary: Investors are testing whether safety-driven development restraint could weaken nearly $800 billion in projected 2026 hyperscaler capital spending. No concrete order cancellations have emerged, and some analysts say credible guardrails may support demand.

stories.headline: Supreme Court blocks new mail-ballot rule
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court declined to let the Postal Service enforce new envelope, barcode and voter-list requirements before the November midterms. Two justices dissented; litigation over the rule continues.

stories.headline: Houthi attacks widen as Hormuz talks stall
stories.summary: Houthis launched new missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia while Gulf states postponed Iran talks. Riyadh says 13 civilians were wounded; conflicting accounts remain over damage to the tanker El Gaia.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine continue energy strikes
stories.summary: Russia struck a Kyiv petrol station and warehouses as Ukraine hit facilities in Russia, one day after President Trump said both sides had agreed not to target energy assets. Russia has not confirmed such an agreement.
